cells.tense: Something in your keeping is finishing, and you are letting it finish cleanly.
cells.act: trade one thing for one thing, and keep no score
cells.ask: Set a finished arrangement beside one you'd rather have, say the trade out loud to whoever's with you, and walk away without keeping a tally.
cells.core:
You can end something when it's finished — a role you've been living in, a routine that used to fit — without dragging it out or blowing it up on the way. The ending comes from your own sense that it's run its course, so nobody has to be persuaded or managed through it. The room gets lighter, and the weight went down because you set it down.

What makes the clearing cheaper is fairness. Set a finished arrangement beside one you'd rather have, say the trade out loud, and don't start counting afterwards. What you give up is the comfort of the familiar setup; what you get is the hours in it. Things end where they end, and nobody has to pay twice.

cells.verb: letting something fully end so the next thing can begin

cells.tense: You will keep clearing things out, and the ending will land before any of it has had its turn.
cells.act: let yourself be reached by what they are carrying
cells.ask: Stay beside whatever you're set on ending and let what it has been carrying for the people in it reach you before you say the word.
cells.core:
Closed before it lived. From where you stand the thing has nothing left to give, and calling it over feels like air coming in. Those inside it get a door swinging shut on them, and after enough turns of that they stop bringing you what they'd rather keep — they've learned how much time anything gets.

What's thin isn't resolve, it's contact with what's still alive here. Let yourself be reached by what the thing is holding, and stay with it before you end it — what it has been carrying matters to someone who isn't you. The endings you make afterwards will be right, and fewer, and the ones you keep will still be there when you look again.

cells.tense: A way of living has finished, and you are still keeping the door behind you propped open.
cells.act: move toward the thing you want, one step, today
cells.ask: Take one step today toward something that pulls you — a call, a walk, a page — before you feel ready for it.
cells.core:
The shape underneath the routine stopped, and you're still showing up to it. The habit is there and the familiar sentences go on being spoken, and nothing alive is left in the slot. Staying doesn't read as loyalty to anyone in it; it reads mostly as an hour that could have gone to something growing.

Movement gets you out, and it doesn't wait for clarity. Go where the feeling is already pulling, take one step today, before you feel ready. The old slot fills with something in motion, and no announcement is needed. Not a funeral you're avoiding — a place at the table still set, and a person who could be sitting there doing what they want.

cells.tense: A way of meeting is quietly loosening, and your hand is the one letting it go.
cells.act: put a date, a place, a container on it
cells.ask: Mark the next meeting in your own book as the last one you'll keep — a circle around the day, no announcement — and let that be the end of it.
cells.core:
A way of meeting or arranging things is thinning — you renew it less, then not at all — and if someone put the question to you straight you'd shrug it off. There is a hand at work. So far the hand hasn't signed anything, which means nobody, yourself included, knows where the floor is.

Give the loosening an edge you can see. Mark the next meeting in your own book as the last one you'll keep, circle the day, and let that be it. What the others can already feel becomes a thing with an edge on it. You stop being the one who might bring it back, and it settles into what happened rather than what might still.
cells.sheetLine: What's ending is ending by your hand.
